invariant: ANY LLM-facing tool in lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/tools.ts that returns contract text claimed or usable as CURRENT operative evidence MUST set ToolExecutionOutcome.evidenceUnresolved = true whenever that evidence cannot be positively established as current operative truth. This must never depend on the model reading/understanding a status string inside the tool's own JSON payload (that is metadata, not enforcement) - evidenceUnresolved is the one machine-readable, independently-checkable flag ToolRunner.run copies onto ToolCallLogEntry, and that compile.ts/verify.ts actually gate VERIFIED/COMPLETED on via `.some(entry => entry.evidenceUnresolved)`.

confirmedDefect.rootCause: getOperativeProvision computed a real OperativeProvisionView.status (a genuine 4-value OperativeStateStatus: OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED/PARTIAL/REVIEW_REQUIRED/CONFLICTED, from resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence/operative-state.ts's own buildProvisionView) and returned it in the response PAYLOAD, but its execute() body never translated that status into ToolExecutionOutcome.evidenceUnresolved. Its sibling getDefinition, computing the analogous DefinitionEvidenceStatus via resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence, DID correctly set `outcome.evidenceUnresolved = !resolution.isCurrentTruth`. Two near-identical tools independently deciding whether/how to set the flag is exactly how one of them silently skipped it - not a one-off typo, a structural gap in HOW the flag was derived.
confirmedDefect.exploitConfirmed: tests/certification/part-b-final-recert-fix2-independent.test.ts - a genuinely OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED section, reached only via a real getOperativeProvision tool call (never pre-loaded in the context bundle), reached a persisted SemanticTruthRecord.trustStatus of VERIFIED via a real Postgres round-trip. Confirmed pre-fix by running that file: evidenceUnresolved was undefined/falsy, compile status was COMPLETED, verify.ts status was VERIFIED_*, and trustStatus persisted VERIFIED.

optionA_runnerLevelGenericWrapper.description: Derive evidenceUnresolved generically inside ToolRunner.run, outside every tool's own execute() body, by inspecting the returned result payload's own status-shaped field.
optionA_runnerLevelGenericWrapper.decision: REJECTED as infeasible without an invasive redesign, per the spec's own fallback criterion.
optionA_runnerLevelGenericWrapper.reasoning: Each tool's result payload shape genuinely differs: getOperativeProvision keys off a top-level `status` field (OperativeStateStatus vocabulary); getDefinition keys off `evidenceStatus`+`isCurrentTruth` (a richer, distinct DefinitionEvidenceStatus vocabulary); getParentClause/getSiblingClauses/getReferencedProvision key off a per-response or per-item `supersessionStatus` field (NodeSupersessionStatus vocabulary, and getSiblingClauses returns an ARRAY of them, one per sibling); getChildren keys off `parentSupersessionStatus`; getRelatedAmendments keys off `status` again but with a materially different response shape (an amendment chain, not current text). ToolRunner.run receives only `unknown` JSON at the point evidenceUnresolved would need to be derived - making it generic there would require either (a) a second, parallel per-tool-name lookup table duplicating exactly the same per-tool knowledge the tool's own execute() body already has, defeating the point of centralizing, or (b) a runtime schema-sniffing heuristic (look for any field literally named '*Status' or '*status') that is fragile, silently wrong for a field that happens to share a name but a different vocabulary, and impossible to statically type-check.

optionB_sharedHelperPerTool.description: One canonical boolean-mapping helper function every CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE tool's own execute() body calls to derive evidenceUnresolved, rather than each tool deciding independently which status values count as safe.
implementation: New exported function `isConfirmedCurrentOperativeEvidence(status: CurrentOperativeEvidenceStatus): boolean` added to lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/operative-state.ts (co-located with getNodeSupersessionStatus and the other operative-state primitives it composes with).
CurrentOperativeEvidenceStatus = OperativeStateStatus | NodeSupersessionStatus - the ONLY two status vocabularies a CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE tool in this codebase can produce.

Returns true only for the two literal 'positively confirmed current' values (OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED, CURRENT_OPERATIVE); every other value (CONFLICTED, PARTIAL, REVIEW_REQUIRED, KNOWN_SUPERSEDED, UNKNOWN_SUPERSESSION_STATUS) fails closed to false.

getDefinition already derives evidenceUnresolved from its own resolution.isCurrentTruth boolean (resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence's own internal, equivalent single-purpose mapping for the richer DefinitionEvidenceStatus vocabulary) - left untouched; it was never the defect, and forcing it through the new helper would mean widening/lossy-collapsing DefinitionEvidenceStatus's 6-value taxonomy for no safety benefit.

Every CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE tool that consults an OperativeProvisionView.status or a NodeSupersessionStatus directly now derives evidenceUnresolved from isConfirmedCurrentOperativeEvidence(status) - never a second, independent judgment call.

booleanVsEnumDecision.decision: Retained the existing evidenceUnresolved: boolean field on ToolExecutionOutcome/ToolCallLogEntry - did NOT replace it with a full evidenceTrust enum.
booleanVsEnumDecision.reasoning: The boolean already enforces equivalent behavior once its DERIVATION is fixed (the actual defect): compile.ts and verify.ts both gate on `.some(entry => entry.evidenceUnresolved)`, a pure OR reduction that does not need to distinguish CONFLICTED from PARTIAL from KNOWN_SUPERSEDED to make the correct fail-closed decision - all of them must produce the same downstream consequence (never VERIFIED/COMPLETED off that evidence alone). The RICHER status (OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED, etc.) is never discarded - it remains fully disclosed in the tool's own result payload and in outputSummary for human/model context; only the machine trust-gating signal is intentionally collapsed to a boolean, which is exactly what the gating logic needs and no more.

toolsChanged.change: found-view branch now sets evidenceUnresolved = !isConfirmedCurrentOperativeEvidence(view.status) [THE CONFIRMED DEFECT]; raw base-document fallback branch now ALSO consults supersessionIndex via getNodeSupersessionStatus (previously never consulted at all - a second, independently-found gap in the same tool) and sets evidenceUnresolved accordingly, mirroring getDefinition's own base-document-fallback discipline (KNOWN_SUPERSEDED -> legacyStatus OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL).

now sets evidenceUnresolved = !isConfirmedCurrentOperativeEvidence(resolved.supersessionStatus) - previously disclosed supersessionStatus in the payload but never derived the machine flag at all (a real, independently-found registry-audit gap, same class as getOperativeProvision's).

now sets evidenceUnresolved = rendered.some(sibling => !isConfirmedCurrentOperativeEvidence(sibling.supersessionStatus)) - fails closed for the WHOLE call if ANY one sibling's own text is not confirmed current, never masked by other siblings that are.
both resolution branches (fromNodeId-relative and absolute-ref-loop) now set evidenceUnresolved = !isConfirmedCurrentOperativeEvidence(resolved.supersessionStatus).

now sets evidenceUnresolved = !isConfirmedCurrentOperativeEvidence(parentSupersession.status) - defensive/belt-and-suspenders: this tool returns only short heading text (not full provision text), but headings can themselves carry economics (e.g. a basket amount in a heading), and the tool is already declared CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE.

now sets evidenceUnresolved = !isConfirmedCurrentOperativeEvidence(view.status) - defensive/belt-and-suspenders: this tool's primary content (the amendment chain's oldText/newText) is already explicitly historical per entry, but it discloses the provision's own aggregate view.status and is declared CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE.
UNCHANGED - already correctly derives evidenceUnresolved = !resolution.isCurrentTruth. Used as the contrast/regression baseline throughout the fresh attack matrix.

enforcementBackstop: tests/contract-model/semantic-tools-operative-state-discipline.test.ts's pre-existing registry-iterating test (every registered tool must declare a real operativeStateDiscipline, a TypeScript-mandatory field) remains the compile-time backstop for a future new tool skipping classification entirely. A NEW describe block in that same file (HEADROOM OPEN-2) is the runtime backstop for a future CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE tool skipping evidenceUnresolved derivation: it iterates the 7 CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE tools that return interpretable text and asserts a CURRENT case (falsy) and an UNRESOLVED/SUPERSEDED case (true) for each. This is a human-discipline backstop, not a compiler-enforced one (option A was rejected precisely because no compiler-enforceable generic derivation exists here) - the registry test is the safety net for that remaining step.
